records.quote: Case I : θ1 < θ2. Let X~GIW(α, θ1, λ, β) and Y~GIW(α, θ2, λ, β). Then gX(y)/gY(y) = [α^{θ1}θ1(1 − α^{θ2})[1 − (1 − α)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ2+1}] / [α^{θ2}θ2(1 − α^{θ1})[1 − (1 − α)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ1+1}]. Since θ1 < θ2, d/dx[gX(y)/gY(y)] < 0. Hence, gX(y)/gY(y) is decreasing in y. That is X ≤lr Y. The remaining statement follow from the implication (32).

Then gX(y)/gY(y) = [α1^θ(1 − α1)(1 − α2^θ)/(α2^θ(1 − α2)(1 − α1^θ))] · [[1 − (1 − α2)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]/[1 − (1 − α1)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]]^{θ+1}. Since α2 < α1, d/dx[gX(y)/gY(y)] = −(α1 − α2)(θ + 1)(λ/y)^β(β/y)e^{−(λ/y)^β}[1 − (1 − α2)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^θ/[1 − (1 − α1)e^{−(λ/y)^β}]^{θ+2} < 0. Hence, gX(y)/gY(y) is decreasing in y. That is X ≤lr Y.
